operations.evidence: Financial Year combined with Financial Quarter identifies when offences were initially recorded
the field is a recording/reporting period and not an exact incident timestamp
Quarter 1 is April to June, Quarter 2 July to September, Quarter 3 October to December, and Quarter 4 January to March
quarter labels must be interpreted within the stated financial year
Force Name identifies the police force area in which the offence was recorded
generally does not guarantee an exact occurrence location or parcel
CSP Name identifies the Community Safety Partnership area in which offences were recorded
CSP geography is not a parcel boundary
Offence codes map to offence descriptions, subgroups and groups
classification hierarchy must not be treated as independent additive categories without code-level checks
each row contains a count for a specified offence code, area, financial year and financial quarter
a row is an aggregate count and not an individual crime record
PFA tables include quarterly centrally recorded fraud data from Action Fraud, Cifas and Financial Fraud UK from 2011/12
central fraud rows are not territorial-force parcel observations
the geographic reference table maps CSP values to police force areas, regions and ONS codes
the ONS code identifies the CSP and does not identify a property
the offence reference table provides old pre-July-2013 and new post-July-2013 offence groups and subgroups
time-series joins must retain the applicable classification version
figures in the PRC tables are additive
addition is valid only after matching area, offence and period dimensions
British Transport Police data are excluded from CSP-level police recorded crime data
CSP data must not be presented as complete national coverage
offence code 49A was introduced separately in April 2013
the reconstructed back series is not uniformly observed
residential and non-residential burglary replaced domestic and non-domestic burglary from April 2017
the classification change requires a time-series break or mapping
residential burglary was split into residential home and residential unconnected buildings from April 2023
the newer subcategories should not be silently backfilled
low-volume crime rates are typically calculated per 1,000 population using ONS population estimates
rate denominators must match the geographic and temporal scope
quarterly figures are revised each quarter when crimes are transferred to another force or cancelled
a published quarter is not necessarily immutable
negative quarterly values can occur before 2019 because forces deducted transferred or cancelled crimes from cumulative monthly returns
negative values are correction mechanics and not negative incidents
the outcomes framework was introduced in April 2013 and replaced the detections regime
pre-framework detections are not directly equivalent to later outcomes
the broader outcomes framework was fully introduced in April 2014
cross-framework comparisons require explicit mapping
quarterly outcomes open data have been published since 2014/15
publication cadence does not imply all investigations are final
the recorded-period view links outcomes to individual recorded crimes
open investigations must not be forced into a final outcome
each quarter's linked outcome data provides an incomplete picture when first published
initial snapshots should not be interpreted as final cohort performance
linked outcome data is particularly useful for tracking sexual offences that can take a long time to reach a final outcome
later revisions are required for mature comparisons
outcomes closed in the latest period can relate to crimes recorded in previous years
the numerator and same-year crime denominator may cover different cohorts
closed-period outcome rates can exceed 100% for some low-volume crime types
rates over 100% must not be treated as impossible data or direct performance scores
the Home Office receives monthly crime, outcome and transferred/cancelled data from police forces
the data flow does not cover all centrally recorded fraud and cybercrime
Home Office statisticians analyse submissions and return anomaly or error reports to the relevant force for validation or correction
quality assurance can identify issues but does not guarantee error-free data
before publication, Home Office data are returned to all forces for confirmation against their systems
force confirmation is a verification control, not independent remeasurement
the Home Office Data Hub allows forces to provide record-level detail on offences
record-level administrative data are still subject to recording and revision limitations
a small number of forces supply an aggregated Crimsec4 return monthly
mixed source formats can limit uniform record-level analysis
the framework was designed to recognise the full range of disposals and avoid favouring one outcome
no outcome category should be ranked automatically as universally better
